text:
Aria: Heads-up: Prospect HeliosNet wants a hosted POC environment. Requirements: per-integration hosted API keys, IP allowlist (198.51.100.10/32), automated daily rotation, audit export to customer S3, and a hard kill at end of 7-day window. Theyre internal infra folks, so security will want the exact rotation scheme.

Diego: I'll create per-integration ephemeral keys. For consistency we'll do 48h TTL with automatic rotation job that overlaps by 2h to prevent mid-window invalidations. Using `redwoodctl` sample:```bash
redwoodctl keys create \
  --type=ephemeral \
  --scopes=generation,embeddings \
  --allowed-ips=198.51.100.10/32 \
  --ttl=48h \
  --note="HeliosNet-<integration>"
```Keep tokens in their vault; send over our secure transfer link.

Sam: Compliance note: need issuance audit events, rotation logs, and revocation events sent to their S3. Provide them an ARN and we'll ask for an IAM role with PutObject. Also confirm they don't require CMK.

Diego: Plan for rotation automation: job creates new key, places new token in staging vault, updates their integration config (if they want), then revokes old key after 2h. I'll own the flow.

Aria: Great. Ops-bot: schedule revoke-on-expiry reminder.

ops-bot: Task scheduled: HeliosNet POC key expiry reminder -> 1717063200.

Diego: I'll draft a short handoff doc with curl examples, revoke instructions, and how to request extensions.

Aria: Thanks. If security needs more, cc Jo from security.
